To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified the major oxidation products of tryptophan residues in a monoclonal antibody as kynurenin, N-formylkynamine and hydroxytrytpthophan and that these tryptophan derivatives, but not methione or histidine derivatives, are responsible for color change of the antibody.
tryptophanyl chromophores, but not methoninyl and histidinyl chromophores, are responsible for the color changes in light-irradiation and heat-stressed antibody drug product in formulation.
tryptophans are the major source of chromophores responsible of the color change of the mAb in light-irradiation and heat-stressed samples, and the color changes are not due to the excipients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of degradation of a mAb in liquid formulation under the influence of near UV-visible light irradiation and heat stress.
the identification of the degradation products responsible for the color changes in light-irradiation and heat-stressed antibody samples.
the development of a new peptide mapping method for the identification of tryptophan-containing chromophores responsible in mAb drug product.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the color change in the light-irradiation- and heat-stressed drug product is due to the tryptophans oxidation products, Kyn, NFK, and OH-Trp.
color change in stressed antibody formulations is due to the formation of tryptophan-containing chromophores.

the color change in mAb drug product is due to tryptophan oxidative degradation products, but not histidine or methionine oxidation products, and the new oxidation product with loss of hydrogen on tryptophan is responsible for the heat-induced color change in mAbs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed new methods for the characterization of the degradation products responsible for the color changes in mAb drug products.

tryptophans are very important amino acids for the stability of therapeutic mAbs, and the tryptophans should be carefully considered during the development of a mAb drug product to avoid the color change.
the tryptophanyl oxidation products were responsible for the mAb drug product color change.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tryptophans are the most susceptible residues to oxidation in a monoclonal antibody and are responsible for the yellow coloration of the antibody upon exposure to light.

it is important to identify the chromophore responsible for color change, and the new peptide mapping technique can be a very useful tool to identify the tryptophans responsible for the color changes in the stressed mAb drug products.
